title: Atlas Crossing Partners | Vanguard Auto | LBO Model — Overview
summary: LBO model for Vanguard Auto Parts (Atlas Crossing Partners Fund III), underwriting a July 2020 platform entry at an 11.0× EV/EBITDA entry multiple on $19.8M LTM EBITDA (entry EV: $218M). The model projects a 7-year hold to FY2027E exit, incorporating two add-on acquisitions (Precision, FleetFirst). Base case exit EV of $431.2M at 11.0× on $39.2M EBITDA generates a gross MOIC of 3.34× and gross IRR of ~18.8% (net MOIC ~2.74×, net IRR ~15.0%). The debt structure consists of a $99M Senior TL (5.0× EBITDA at 6.8%) and $29.7M Sub/Mezz PIK (1.5× EBITDA at 11.5%), with $89.3M of Atlas Crossing equity (~41% of EV). Revenue grows from $112M at entry to $211.5M at exit; EBITDA margin expands modestly from 17.7% to 18.5%. The model includes full income statement, debt schedule with amortization/PIK accretion, and a returns sensitivity table across five EBITDA and exit multiple scenarios.

growth_drivers: Organic revenue growth ~7-10% annually through mid-hold
EBITDA margin expansion from operational leverage
Excess cash flow sweep accelerating debt paydown
risks: High initial leverage (6.5× Debt/EBITDA at entry)
PIK debt accreting from $29.7M to $70.9M by exit, adding to net debt
Revenue decline in FY2021A (-6.4% YoY) highlights cyclicality risk
Integration risk from two add-on acquisitions
Automotive aftermarket sector exposure to cyclicality
